O1.citation: “The run is invalid because the runner saw the case bar… Discard both its artifact and grade.” Also: “Report only the fresh run’s result.”

O2.citation: The artifact requires a “fresh, context-free runner” and “a separate judge,” but says to give the runner “only the case input,” omitting the required skill instructions.

O3.citation: “Remove only runner-created files and revert only runner-authored changes. If ownership of any change is uncertain, do not delete or revert it.”

O4.citation: It requires inspecting the checkout “regardless of sandboxing,” but never requires a throwaway sandbox with no writable live checkout for future runs.

S1.citation: Smell absent: “Discard both its artifact and grade” and “Report only the fresh run’s result.”

S2.citation: Smell absent: “Start a fresh, context-free runner for that case.”

S3.citation: Smell absent: recovery uses targeted removal and restoration only, and directs: “If ownership of any change is uncertain, do not delete or revert it.”

S4.citation: Smell absent: “Inspect and clean the live checkout again after the rerun, regardless of sandboxing.”

rationale: The artifact correctly invalidates the contaminated run, preserves unrelated checkout work, uses fresh runner/judge sessions, and mandates post-run inspection. It is incomplete because the fresh runner is not explicitly given the skill instructions and future runs are not explicitly moved to a throwaway sandbox without writable access to the live checkout.
